scope: Proposition 5.2 (Invariant spaces for the exact Dirichlet maps) of the manuscript “A Three-Dimensional Counterexample to Integer-Degree Harmonic Dimension Comparison” (preprints/A-Three-Dimensional-Counterexample-to-Integer-Degree-Harmonic-Dimension-Comparison-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 361 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6c7b86f0f59fcdb9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: After increasing J, there is a fixed κ < 1 such that, uniformly in the controls, TQL = O(δj), TLL = diag(αi(j)−1 ) + O(δj), TLQ = o(1), ∥TQQ∥ ≤ κτj. (5.10) There is a unique family of graph maps Vj : Rp → Qj, among families in one fixed sufficiently small operator ball, such that Tj maps graphj+1 Vj+1 = {ιj+1c + Vj+1c : c ∈ Rp } isomorphically onto graphj Vj. They satisfy ∥Vj∥ ≤ Cδj. For each fixed j, Vj is continuous in operator norm as a function of the complete control sequence with its countable product topology. The outward matrix on these spaces is Aj = (TLL + TLQVj+1)−1 = diag(αi(j)) + O(δj), TLQVj+1 = o(δj). (5.11) It too is continuous in the product topology.
